text_blocks.snippet: Motor neurone disease (MND) can be genetic, but the majority of cases are sporadic, meaning they occur without a family history. While about 10-15% of MND cases are attributed to genetic mutations, over 100 different genes have been identified as potential contributors. For cases with a known genetic cause, inheritance patterns can vary, with some following autosomal dominant patterns where a child has a 50% chance of inheriting the condition if a parent has it.
